subject: Urgent: production p99 regressions and errors impacting BlueWave – immediate action required
messages:
From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@bluewaveanalytics.com>

Cc: ops@bluewaveanalytics.com
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: sudden p99 spikes since Friday deploy – production impact

Hi team,

Since Friday evening's change we are seeing frequent p99 latency spikes (10s-30s) and a rise in 5xx errors on the hosted API route we use (model: rwd-large-quant). This is affecting our realtime scoring pipeline — retries are piling up and downstream throughput has dropped ~40%.

Examples (timestamps UTC):
- req_id: b1a7cd9e @ 2026-02-27T23:42:07Z -> 28s p99 and eventual 502
- req_id: b1a8f1c2 @ 2026-02-28T01:10:13Z -> 12s p99 then timeout

We raised an internal incident and are throttling client calls but need Redwood to investigate urgently. Can you confirm if there were infra changes Friday evening or any known regressions? We will need an expected ETA for a fix and whether you can failover us to a stable model/version.

Attaching a short list of sample request IDs and a graph from our side. Please loop in whoever owns runtime/inference.

Thanks,
Sara Lewis
Head of Platform Reliability
BlueWave Analytics

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: sudden p99 spikes since Friday deploy – production impact

Quick update from runtime triage (initial findings):

What I did:
- Pulled the sample req IDs and replayed them against the hosted pool in canary.
- Checked GPU metrics, allocator stats, and runtime logs across the pool nodes that handle rwd-large-quant.

Findings (short):
- We are seeing progressive GPU memory fragmentation on the NeMo-derived execution path for rwd-large-quant under the specific sequence length and batching patterns in BlueWave's workload. Memory footprints drift up across long-lived worker processes and eventually trigger soft OOMs that lead to large tail latencies (30s+) while the runtime attempts recovery (freeing KV caches, partial GC).
- The failures align with our Friday push that included a patch to kernel selection heuristics (intended to reduce latency for short sequences). The patch changes allocation churn in a corner-case with interleaved long and short sequences.

Immediate mitigations we can do now (order of execution):
1) Temporarily route BlueWave traffic to rwd-medium (lower mem pressure) — trivial routing change, <15m to apply.
2) Restart long-lived worker processes in the affected pool during a rolling window to reclaim fragmented memory — needs a short maintenance window, expected 20-25m with canary first.
3) Revert the kernel-selection heuristic change for affected pool (hotfix) — I can cut the rollback and test on canary; approximately 90m to validate + roll out.

Longer-term fixes:
- Patch allocator to do periodic compaction/defrag on idle cycles (in progress; target sprint 2).
- Add better pre-emptive health checks for fragmentation and auto-bounce before soft OOMs.

Attachments: engine-investigation-notes.txt, p99-trend-graph.png (internal graphs).

I'll start the routing fallback if BlueWave approves; otherwise we'll schedule the rolling restart immediately (we should avoid full pool drain during business hours if possible).

-Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@bluewaveanalytics.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: sudden p99 spikes since Friday deploy – production impact

Sara — thanks for raising this. Two things we propose immediately to reduce customer impact:

1) Failover: route you to rwd-medium for the next 24 hours while Rishi validates and rolls back the kernel-selection change on the rwd-large-quant pool. Pros: quick, low risk. Cons: slight reduction in output quality for a subset of prompts (we'll share diff samples).

2) Rolling bounce: we will schedule a rolling restart of the affected worker processes beginning at 02:00 PT (canary then staged) to recover fragmented memory without a full outage. Estimated customer-facing downtime: none; transient increase in tail while instances warm.

Proposed timeline (subject to your sign-off):
- 11:30 PT: short incident sync (15m) to confirm failover decision and share runbook.
- 12:00 PT: apply routing change if approved.
- 13:30 PT: start canary restart, validate, then continue staged restarts.

I'll set up a 30-minute customer incident review and provide a post-incident summary with root cause, actions, and SLO impact. Sean — can you confirm whether we should simultaneously open a formal credit request for this account if impact > 2 hours?

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: bluewave-additional-logs.zip
